classes.note: Under the 1946 Constitution the vice president was elected on a separate ballot on the presidential election day; since 1966 the vice president runs on the president's ticket.

classes.name: Vice-gubernatorial elections (separate ballot, 1947 to 1965)
classes.note: States whose constitutions created a vice governor elected it on its own ballot, on the gubernatorial election day, until the 1966 indirect elections; since 1982 the vice governor runs on the governor's ticket. Not every state had the office, so this class has no enumerated counts.

classes.name: Indirect presidential elections (Congress and the electoral college)
classes.note: Presidents chosen by Congress (1964, 1966, and 1969) or by the electoral college of Congress and state delegates (1974, 1978, and 1985), with each member's vote recorded in the congressional journal. Also the presidents chosen by the constituent assemblies of 1891 and 1934, which the court's chronology does not list.

classes.name: Direct presidential elections of the First Republic (1894 to 1930)
classes.note: The 1891 Constitution had the president and vice president elected by direct vote on 1 March of the last year of the four-year term, counted by Congress; the 1919 election followed President-elect Rodrigues Alves's death. Results are in the congressional counting reports.

cadence.runoff_rule: Congress chooses between the top two when no one has an absolute majority

classes.name: Chamber of Deputies and Senate elections of the First Republic (1890 to 1930)
classes.note: Deputies were elected by the states every three years by direct vote, and senators (three per state, nine-year terms) one third at a time; each chamber verified its own members' returns, published in its annals.

classes.name: Chamber of Deputies of the Empire (1824 to 1889)
classes.note: Two-stage elections (parish voters chose electors, who chose deputies) until the 1881 Saraiva Law made them direct. Senators were appointed by the emperor from lists of three the same electors drew up, and provincial assemblies (from 1834) were elected the same way; all of them published only in parliamentary annals and provincial reports.

classes.name: Supplementary gubernatorial and Senate elections
classes.note: When the electoral courts annul an election winning more than half the votes, or remove an elected governor or senator, a new direct election follows (Electoral Code art. 224). The TSE's general-election files carry two: Mato Grosso's Senate seat on 2020-11-15 and Roraima's governorship on 2026-06-21. The gubernatorial elections of Amazonas (2017-08-06 and 2017-08-27) and Tocantins (2018-06-03 and 2018-06-24) are in its calendars but not its files.

classes.name: Supplementary municipal elections (mayors and councils)
classes.note: New elections the regional electoral courts call when a mayor's election is annulled or the elected ticket is removed (Electoral Code art. 224), and rarely for a council. Counted per first round from the TSE's municipal files, which carry 646 from 2004 to 2026 (635 for mayor and 11 for council; 9 more were runoffs). A council's indirect election of a mayor when both offices fall vacant in the term's last two years is not counted here.

classes.name: State plebiscites and referendums
classes.note: Plebiscites on dividing a state are called by Congress (Constitution art. 18, § 3, and Law 9.709 of 1998) and run by the Electoral Justice for the state's voters: Pará voted on 11 December 2011 on creating Carajás and Tapajós, two questions. Other state consultations follow the state constitution.

dates.quote: consultas plebiscitárias sobre a divisão do Estado do Pará para a criação do Estado do Carajás e/ou do Estado do Tapajós, convocadas por meio dos Decretos Legislativos nº 136/2011 e nº 137/2011
dates.note: The resolution names the two questions; the date is the polling day the TSE announced, to be confirmed against the results when loaded.

classes.name: Municipal plebiscites and referendums
classes.note: Plebiscites on creating, merging, or splitting municipalities (Constitution art. 18, § 4), run by the regional electoral courts, and since Constitutional Amendment 111 of 2021 local questions a council sends to the court at least 90 days before a municipal election, voted with it (art. 14, § 12). The TSE lists municipal plebiscites held with the 2016 and 2018 elections; five municipalities voted on local questions on 6 October 2024 (Belo Horizonte, Dois Lajeados, Governador Edison Lobão, São Luís, and São Luiz).

classes.name: Fernando de Noronha District Council
classes.note: Seven district councillors elected by direct vote for four years with the general elections, run by the Pernambuco regional electoral court; the state appoints the district's administrator. 3,701 voters in 2026.

classes.name: Child protection council elections (conselhos tutelares)
classes.note: Every municipality has at least one five-member conselho tutelar, elected by the municipality's voters on one national day every four years, the first Sunday of October after the presidential election (2015, 2019, and 2023; next 2027). The municipal children's rights council runs it under a municipal law, with voting machines lent by the electoral courts; over 1.5 million people voted in more than 5,000 municipalities in 2023.
classes.disposition_reason: No central publisher: each municipality's children's rights council declares its own results, and neither the electoral courts nor the human rights ministry publishes candidate votes.

classes.name: Justices of the peace
classes.note: The 1988 Constitution (art. 98, II) provides for a paid justice of the peace elected by direct vote for four years; states have not organized the elections, and the courts keep appointing them.
classes.disposition_reason: No election held: the direct elections art. 98, II, provides for await state laws, and justices of the peace are appointed meanwhile.

classes.name: Mercosur Parliament
classes.note: The 2005 protocol foresaw direct elections; Paraguay and Argentina held them, but Brazil's members are still chosen by Congress from among its own.
classes.disposition_reason: Never held in Brazil: Congress appoints Brazil's members of the Mercosur Parliament.

classes.name: Party primaries, professional councils, school principals, and university rectors
classes.note: Party prévias, elections to the bar association and the professional councils, school-community elections of public school principals, and university rector consultations.
classes.disposition_reason: Party-internal, professional, or workplace votes that no electoral court runs or certifies.
